recording: self-contained runtime gate (code/gate.py, a copy of experiments/2026-11-18-range-pruning/code/gate.py (amendments 1 and 3)) and self-recorded manifests; not recorded by the team runtime
question: Does running several queries in flight (one CUDA stream per query) raise the throughput of the exact pruned scorer with the theta-filtered merge, with the same schedule and answers, and how does it compare with the exhaustive range scorer's best batch mode?
hypothesis: The pruned scorer runs five dependent kernels per query, two of them single-block (seed selection) or short (bounds, compaction), and its persistent scoring grid often has little work (6.3% of ranges at range size 256). One query at a time leaves the GPU partly idle; with 32 queries in flight on separate streams, one query's small kernels and idle gaps overlap others' scoring, so throughput should rise (by an unknown factor; not more than the inverse of one query's busy fraction). The range scorer's batched mode reached 1.20x its sequential throughput in run 20261117-cuda5-full-03; the pruned scorer starts about 2.7x faster per query
contract: GSP-CAP32-U32GUARDED-NUMERIC-TIES-v1; uint8 impacts, prepared integer query weights, uint32 accumulation under the conservative-bound guard, reported as uint64; ties by original numeric passage ID; all passages eligible
exactness: Each query owns every mutable object (bounds, marks and epoch, work list, state, candidates, heads, scratch, output, stream, pinned results); the kernels are cuda_range_prune_tm.cu's, unchanged, so each query's schedule and answers are those of the single-query scorer

inputs.rule: checked by whole-file SHA-256 before any scoring
inputs.provenance: W512 and W256 built on cuda5 from the pinned GSP by range_bitpack_tool (`build GSP OUT SIZE positions`, uniform ranges), compiled from src/range_bitpack_tool.cpp and src/range_bitpack.h as last changed in 223cf4b; the same binary regenerated the pinned W1024 index with an equal hash

fixed.host: cuda5 (RTX 4070, UUID GPU-ab7b89ba-5664-fd05-e352-a4bc034e5ff7; host thread on CPU 0, local allocation)

implementations.v2batch: src/cuda_range_batch.cu unchanged (#15): multi-query driver for the exhaustive range scorer v2 (range size 1024), modes sequential and batched
implementations.tmb: src/cuda_range_prune_tmb.cu: multi-query driver for cuda_range_prune_tm.cu (64 seeds), modes sequential (one query at a time) and streams (all queries of a batch launched on their own streams before any is collected)
implementations.prior_binaries: range_bitpack_tool (fixture index builder) from run 20261118-cuda5-da-01, hash-checked

timing_boundary: Per batch, host wall clock from the start of the batch (all its queries complete in host memory beforehand) to the last query's ordered top-k in pinned host memory (batch_wall_ms), including every launch, stream and event; per query, completion_ms from the batch start. Schedule statistics, checks and output writes are after the boundary

timing.order: every configuration once per pass, three passes with rotation offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
timing.before_each_process: timing processes only: wait (30 s polls, bounded by the deadline) until no foreign GPU process is active, 7000 MiB of device memory are free and other users' CPU use is at most CPU_LIMIT cores
timing.sampling: every 0.5 s during each process: nvidia-smi compute processes on the GPU and machine CPU time from /proc minus the scorer and the sampler; sampler on CPU 15
timing.eligibility: a timing process is ineligible if a foreign GPU process was active (per-process SM or memory utilisation above 0, or listed but not reported) in its released phase, its own was not sampled, or other users' CPU use averaged more than CPU_LIMIT cores; a non-zero exit while another GPU process was sampled is a contended failure (ineligible); any other failure stops the run
timing.replacement: ineligible processes are kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced without a count limit; the run stops at a 12-hour deadline and can be resumed from the same commit
timing.cpu_limit_rationale: Every configuration is a GPU scorer with one host thread on CPU 0 (sampler on CPU 15, 14 other cores). The earlier GPU experiments (range batching, full-collection baselines) had no CPU rule. The CPU-baseline experiment's 1.0 core was first adopted here, but in dry-run dev-prune-01 another user's single-threaded job kept other CPU use at 1.1-2.7 cores for over 15 minutes with no GPU process, which would stall or fail the run without bearing on GPU timing. 4.0 cores is a quarter of the machine. It was set before registration and before any latency from this experiment was read; other users' CPU use is recorded for every process. The GPU rule (no other GPU process sampled) is unchanged
timing.rules_source: the range-pruning experiment's rules with its amendments 1-3 in force from the start

correctness_gate: From the timed source and binaries on the timed host: tests/check_range_batch.py (cuda_range_batch, all modes) and tests/check_range_prune_batch.py (cuda_range_prune_tmb, both modes, batch sizes with partial last batches, answers and the independent schedule model, VERIFY=1 poisoning); two deliberate gate rejections; every configuration once against the CPU reference, with VERIFY=1 for tmb-w256-streams-b32 (in-driver host recomputation of answers and schedule) and v2batch-batched-b32 (in-driver CPU reference); every timing process's answers against the reference; tmb schedules identical across rounds, processes and modes (analysis). Any mismatch stops the run

analysis.per_process_round: throughput = 500 / sum of batch_wall_ms over the round's batches
analysis.primary: tmb-w256-streams-b32 over tmb-w256-sequential-b32 (throughput ratio, paired by process and round; geometric mean)
analysis.secondary: tmb-w256-streams-b32 over v2batch-batched-b32; tmb-w256-streams-b8 over tmb-w256-sequential-b32; tmb-w1024-streams-b32 over tmb-w1024-sequential-b32; tmb-w256-sequential-b32 over v2batch-sequential-b32
analysis.descriptive: median throughput (queries/s); completion latency median, p95, p99
analysis.interval: crossed process/round bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261118, percentile 2.5/97.5; conditional on this session and the calibration queries

decision_rule: streams becomes the pruned scorer's throughput mode (reported with its batch size and completion latency) if the primary interval lies wholly above 1; otherwise the result is reported as negative and one query at a time stays the reference
limits: one host, one GPU (RTX 4070), k = 10, batches formed from consecutive calibration queries with no arrival process
throughput and completion latency trade off: a query in a batch of 32 waits for its batch
shared machine; calibration queries only; held-out untouched
